answer: An anti-Sybil design could anchor identity in an orchard graph instead of stake or documents. Each participant tends one vertex in a lattice of plots, gaining standing only when neighbors confirm season-long work: pruning, grafting, and harvest records that cannot be faked overnight. A crystal lattice key, grown from those confirmations over successive seasons, binds the vertex to one human history. Splitting into many identities means tending many plots at full effort, so cost scales linearly, not cheaply. New vertices start with no voting weight and earn it through auditable seasons.
